findings.description: Unsafe eval usage in SQLAlchemy class resolver allows arbitrary code execution
findings.reasoning: The _class_resolver.__call__ method uses eval() with user-controlled self.arg string and globals() context, allowing arbitrary Python code execution. self.arg comes from relationship() string arguments which could be influenced by attackers if relationship definitions are dynamically generated from untrusted input. No sanitization or validation is performed before eval. This could lead to remote code execution if an attacker can inject malicious strings into relationship definitions.

findings.description: Unsafe exec() usage allows arbitrary code execution via generated __init__ function
findings.reasoning: The code uses exec() on dynamically generated function text (func_text) which comes from untrusted user input via class instrumentation. An attacker who can control the class definition or relationship arguments could inject arbitrary Python code that would be executed via exec(). The locals().copy() environment combined with __name__ makes this a classic code injection vulnerability.
